newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Tajikistan aluminium plant sees 1997 output up.
newsitem.headline: Tajikistan aluminium plant sees 1997 output up.

text.p: Tajikistan's Tursunzade aluminium smelter plans to boost production in 1997 by around 30,000 tonnes to 230,000 tonnes, Interfax news agency quoted the plant's chief engineer Lavrenty Gabrielyan as saying on Friday.

The smelter, which is Tajikistan's main hard currency earner, produced 198,300 tonnes in 1996, down sharply from the 237,500 tonnes it produced in 1995 and just 40 percent of annual capacity of 500,000 tonnes.

During the first three months of this year the smelter produced around 45,000 tonnes of primary aluminium. Output so far this year has fallen behind planned volumes because of power shortages in the former Soviet republic, which has suffered years of civil strife.
But Gabrielyan said that problems with securing alumina, a raw material used to make aluminium, should be eased this year. Ukraine will remain the plant's main alumina supplier in 1997, he said.
